summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of systolic heart failure, diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and morbid obesity was admitted for acute volume overload and bilateral lower extremity ulcers that developed after increased salt intake. He received oral and intravenous diuresis, resulting in an 8-pound weight loss and mild improvement in edema. The ulcers showed no signs of infection, so antibiotics were not started. Podiatry recommended wound care with lac-hydrin and dry dressings. Despite medical recommendations to stay for further diuresis and monitoring, the patient elected to leave the hospital after one night. He was discharged on home medications including torsemide 80 mg daily, with instructions to follow up with his PCP and podiatrist, monitor daily weights, and watch for signs of infection or worsening heart failure.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
